title: Repository supply-chain and contract conformance governance
purpose: Record design-only governance for SBOM generation, dependency licence policy, supply-chain provenance, and contract conformance test prerequisites without scanner implementation, attestation implementation, schema activation, contract test implementation, or readiness claims.

nonClaims: No provenance or attestation system is implemented.
No contract conformance test is implemented.
No generated client pipeline is made ready.
No readiness, staging, production, deployment, compliance, store, release, live-provider, or human-acceptance claim is made.

dependencyStatus.title: Lockfile hygiene
usedFor: SBOM and licence report invalidation trigger

dependencyStatus.title: Contract test standard
usedFor: contract conformance test class and fallback expectations

sbomGenerationProposal.format: CycloneDX JSON is the preferred candidate format for dependency SBOM generation; SPDX JSON remains a review option if owner or legal workflow requires it. This is a format proposal only and does not claim compliance with either standard.
scope: future build artifacts only when a build artifact policy explicitly adds them
generationTrigger: explicit supply-chain validation command in future implementation
sbomGenerationProposal.retention: Retain generated SBOM as an audit artifact tied to source commit, lockfile hash, package manager version, generation tool version, and validation result. The SBOM is a generated report and does not prove functional correctness.
validationExpectations: SBOM input hash matches current package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml.
SBOM package count and root dependencies reconcile with frozen lockfile inputs.
Unknown or stale SBOM state fails closed for supply-chain reporting.
Generated SBOM carries a non-authority marker and source input references.

licencePolicyProposal.scanner: Use a lockfile-derived licence scanner in a future implementation. The scanner must report package name, version, resolved licence expression, source metadata, confidence, and unknown values without making legal conclusions.

thresholds.blockCandidate: No hard block list is defined without owner and legal review; unknown or missing licence data blocks automatic pass.

reviewProcess: Scanner report identifies allow, review-required, unknown, and missing licence classifications.
Review-required dependencies require owner or legal decision before dependency adoption is treated as accepted.
Unknown or missing licence metadata fails closed until resolved or explicitly risk-accepted.
Licence policy changes are governance changes and do not alter semantic authority.
unresolvedLegalQuestions: Which copyleft licences are acceptable for runtime dependencies, development dependencies, generated assets, or tooling only.
Whether transitive optional dependencies require the same review threshold as direct dependencies.
Who owns legal approval and risk acceptance for review-required classifications.
How third-party notice generation will be retained and published if required.
validationExpectations: Licence report derives from frozen lockfile inputs.
Unknown, missing, malformed, or ambiguous licence values fail closed.
Report output records input hashes, scanner version, generated-report non-authority, and owner-review-needed states.

scope: dependency input provenance for package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, package manager version, and override state
build artifact provenance when build artifacts become governed outputs
proof bundle provenance for retained proof-cockpit and evidence bundles
generated report provenance for generated lower-authority reports
metadata: evidence and custody references where relevant
supplyChainProvenanceProposal.storage: Store provenance as a generated audit artifact or manifest adjacent to the artifact it describes, with content hashes and reference-resolution expectations. Provenance records do not replace validators, raw evidence, or semantic authority.
ownerDecisions: Whether to adopt an attestation format and toolchain.
Whether provenance must be signed and which identity signs it.
Whether CI-only provenance is sufficient or local provenance is also required.
Retention class for provenance records and external publication rules.
validationExpectations: Provenance ties to exact inputs and artifacts by hash.
Unknown, stale, unsigned when signing is required, or mismatched provenance fails closed for provenance claims.
Provenance never upgrades generated reports, environment, provider mode, or proof level by implication.

prerequisites: The contract must have active semantic authority or an accepted decision authorising conformance expectations.
If schema-backed, the schema registry lifecycle state must permit validation use.
Generated clients must trace to the exact source contract and generated-client semantics.
Fixtures must identify whether they exercise source contracts, generated projections, provider behaviour, or evidence records.
Planned schemas and planned contracts must be labelled as planned and must not be tested as active authority.

plannedVsActiveSeparation.planned: Planned contracts may have design checks, parse checks, registry consistency checks, and future fixture plans, but they do not create runtime or generated-client conformance obligations.
plannedVsActiveSeparation.active: Active contracts may have conformance tests only after source authority, lifecycle state, fixtures, validators, and failure expectations are defined.
plannedVsActiveSeparation.forbidden: A test must not imply schema activation, generated-client readiness, UI readiness, runtime readiness, or provider readiness from a planned contract.

conformanceMatrix.prerequisite: schema registry lifecycle allows validation and strict JSON parse passes
conformanceMatrix.futureValidation: parse schema and instance JSON, enforce registry lifecycle, and fail closed on unknown lifecycle state

conformanceMatrix.prerequisite: source contract and generated-client mapping are authoritative for the tested surface
conformanceMatrix.futureValidation: verify generated output traces to exact source contract and fails on drift

conformanceMatrix.prerequisite: service catalogue and generated Compose target are in scope
conformanceMatrix.futureValidation: validate catalogue-driven generated output and fail on profile, port, or hardening drift

conformanceMatrix.prerequisite: raw evidence, generated projection, freshness, and custody roles are distinct
conformanceMatrix.futureValidation: fail on generated-report authority upgrade, stale evidence, unknown freshness, or unresolved references

validationProofExpectation: Future implementation must parse JSON strictly where JSON contracts or instances are involved.
Future implementation must respect schema registry lifecycle and must not activate planned schemas by testing them as active.
Ambiguous contract status falls back to design-only or fuller validation, not a pass.
Generated clients require source-to-output trace and drift checks before readiness claims are considered.
